html:
SMTO-EML-0010 — SMTO couldn't hand your email over to the Gateway

GUID: e742b6e8-3a8d-53fa-ba01-2a75042780e7
Slug: email-attachment-staging-failed
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • Before sending, SMTO copies the finished email to the Gateway in pieces. That copy didn't arrive complete or in time, so the Gateway refused it before contacting the mail server. No email went out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on the Gateway you use. If the Gateway disconnected or restarted mid-copy, it loses the partly copied email.
  2. If several emails are being sent at the same time, wait for them to finish first. The Gateway holds only a limited amount of waiting email at once and refuses more.
  3. If the email has large attachments, remove some or use smaller versions. The whole copy must finish within ten minutes, and big messages take longer.
  4. Ask SMTO to send the email again. The mail server was never contacted, so a new attempt won't send recipients a duplicate.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the mail server accepted the message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your Gateways. Mention whether the Gateway was restarted or updated around the time of the error.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway message staging rejected the prepared email (size, SHA-256, quota, ticket owner or expiry, chunk offset or shape, or incomplete data), or an intermediate staging call returned ok:false, before the SMTP exchange began.

What this means

  • Message staging rejects its size/hash/quota, owner/expiry, offset/chunk shape or incomplete digest, or an intermediate email operation reports staging failure. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • Message staging rejects its size/hash/quota, owner/expiry, offset/chunk shape or incomplete digest, or an intermediate email operation reports staging failure.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect staging phase, exact operation ownership, declared byte count and digest without bypassing integrity checks.

How to fix it

  • Check Gateway availability and its log around the begin, chunk, finalize and send calls. Staging rejects sizes of 0 or over 25 MiB, more than 128 concurrent tickets or 64 MiB in total, out-of-order or mismatched chunks, a SHA-256 mismatch, a run/operation owner mismatch, or tickets older than 600 seconds; staged buffers live only in Gateway memory, so a Gateway restart drops them.
  • Check Gateway availability and artifact integrity. Staged bytes must match the declared size, hash, run and operation, and expire after ten minutes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • Finalization verifies the complete intended message under its original authorized run/operation before consumption.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
